natural_language_statement:
Let $m$ be an odd squarefree positive integer and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ be a set every element of which is a unit. If $|A| > \frac{5}{8}\varphi(m)$, then every residue class $x$ modulo $m$, unit or not, can be written $x = a + b + c$ with $a, b, c \in A$ not necessarily distinct. Equivalently $A + A + A = \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$.

The size hypothesis is written `5 * Nat.totient m < 8 * A.card`, which is $|A| > \frac{5}{8}\varphi(m)$ cleared of division so the statement stays in $\mathbb{N}$ without rounding.

The constant is sharp and the inequality has to be strict: at $m = 15$ the set $\{2, 8, 11, 13, 14\}$ has five elements, so $5\varphi(15) = 8 \cdot 5$ exactly, and $1$ is not a sum of three of its elements.
source: Xuancheng Shao, "A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem", Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, arXiv:1206.6139v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139, Corollary 1.5
